title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing p.779). (X,x) is a germ of differentiable surface. V = T_x X is the tangent plane, V* = V\{0}, and S_x = V*/R_{>0} is the circle of tangent directions. D*_x is the punctured germ, understood through the filter of punctured neighbourhoods of x. Equivalence (94), stated just before, says that universal coverings of S_x correspond to universal coverings of the germ D*_x. In modern terms: the real oriented blow-up of x has exceptional circle S_x, and the punctured germ is homotopy-equivalent to that boundary circle.

(95) Naturality statement. Let u be a homeomorphism of X fixing x and differentiable at x (implicitly with du_x invertible). It induces u_{D*} on the punctured germ and u_S on S_x (the latter via du_x). Choose a universal covering of S_x and the associated universal covering of D*_x. Grothendieck claims a canonical bijection between:
- lifts of u_{D*} to the universal covering of D*_x, and
- lifts of u_S to the universal covering of S_x.
This bijection is an isomorphism of T_x-torsors, where T_x is the orientation Z-module of X at x. T_x is canonically the deck group π_1(S_x) ≅ π_1(D*_x) ≅ Z.

He then starts an 'axiomatic description' (marginal heading E) of how (94) and (95) can be built without choices, using only the neighbourhood filter (the 'abstract neighbourhoods' of (122), p.783):
- A_x is the set of arcs of S_x.
- C_x is the set of proper closed convex cones of V (≠ V, ≠ {0}).
- To each arc A or cone C he attaches Ep(A) or ep(C), the corresponding germ of angular sector in D*_x.

The next page completes the construction:
- Sections of the universal covering of S_x over A and sections of the universal covering of D*_x over Ep(A) are both T_x-torsors.
- H(A) = Isom_{T_x} between these two torsors.
- A ↦ H(A) is a functor from the poset A_x to Tors(T_x) whose transition maps are isomorphisms.
- It therefore factors through the groupoid generated by A_x. Since A_x is connected, this yields a single canonical torsor of identifications, i.e. a canonical form of (94).

Purpose: a choice-free, functorial identification of the fundamental groupoid of a punctured surface germ with that of its circle of tangent directions, equivariant under germs of diffeomorphisms. In effect this gives the topological foundation of 'tangential base points' used in the Longue Marche / Teichmüller tower programme.
errors: Implicit hypothesis: u must have invertible differential at x (a local diffeomorphism at x); otherwise u_S is not defined. With du_x invertible, the straight-line homotopy between u and du_x on small punctured discs avoids 0 because u(y) = du_x(y) + o(|y|). This justifies (95).
Transcription line 'rev. universel de \tilde D_x^*' should read 'rev. universel de D_x^*', a slip of pen or transcription.

The sentence defining Ep(A)/ep(C) is incomplete and heavily crossed out; the precise definition of the sector germ (e.g. cone intersected with neighbourhoods, transported via a chart) is not given on this page.

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence between coverings of a punctured surface germ and coverings of its circle of tangent directions
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up / tangential base points (π_1 of punctured disc germ ≅ π_1 of boundary circle of the real blow-up)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, §15) for tangential base points; A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama for real blow-up/log versions
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (base points at boundary circles, 'bouts'); this germ-level formalism is not known to be published

ideas.what: Lifts of a diffeomorphism germ to universal covers of D*_x and of S_x form isomorphic torsors under the orientation module T_x
ideas.modern_name: Equivariance of tangential base point identification under local diffeomorphisms; deck group = orientation local system

ideas.what: Axiomatic construction via arcs of S_x and proper closed convex cones (angular sectors): a functor from the poset of arcs to T_x-torsors, factored through the associated groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Sectorial descent / covering by sectors (as in Stokes/Malgrange–Sibuya sector covers of the real blow-up circle); local system on a poset groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malgrange, Sibuya (sector covers in asymptotic analysis); unsure for this use

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds the identification π_1(punctured germ) ≅ π_1(tangent circle) choice-free, using the poset of arcs of S_x and the corresponding sector germs. This is the topological prototype of Deligne's tangential base points. It is formally the same device (sectors over arcs of the real-blow-up circle) as in Stokes/Malgrange–Sibuya theory, but apparently not linked to it in the literature.
missed.quote: J'ai essayé de donner une description axiomatique de (94) et (95)... A_x l'ens des arcs de S_x ... C_x des cônes convexes fermés propres de V
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical: it documents that Grothendieck independently worked out tangential-base-point foundations, with equivariance under diffeomorphisms, in the topological Teichmüller setting. Mathematically it is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, choice-free foundation of tangential base points for surface germs, predating or parallel to Deligne 1989. Historically interesting, but mathematically elementary and the idea is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'conv. [?] ... propres de V' should read 'l'ens C_{X,x}=C_x des cônes convexes fermés propres de V (≠ V et {0})'.
'rev. universel de \tilde{D}_x^*' should be 'rev. universel de D_x^*'.
'E_p(A) ou e_p(C)' likely denotes the sector germ attached to A or C; 'd'ensemble correspondant de bases de D_x^*' is probably 'le germe d'ensemble correspondant ... de D_x^*'.
'relèvement[?] u^~' should be plural 'relèvements' on both sides of (95).
Margin 'injections (de A ou de C) dans D_x^*' is probably 'germes (de A ou de C) dans D_x^*'.
